Action Plan:
- 1) Suspected labyrinthitis presenting with acute vertigo/dizziness; plan to obtain in-clinic ear examination and vital signs assessment to confirm diagnosis and assess safety.
- 2) Initiate symptomatic treatment and arrange prescription for an oral medication; provide guidance on red-flag symptoms and follow-up with physician.
- 3) Ensure follow-up by the attending doctor for ear inspection; patient to book appointment and contact support to arrange.
- 4) Safety instructions: if new/worsening neurological symptoms (weakness, severe headache) or violent vomiting occur, go to A&E.

- Summary of actions from the consult:
  - Ear examination by a doctor to inspect middle ear status.
  - Blood pressure measurement and gait/walking assessment during waiting period.
  - Start a short course of an unnamed medication (listed as one tablet three times daily for 10 days); route not documented.
  - Provide symptomatic relief with paracetamol as needed.
  - Prescription transmitted to Cross Pharmacy (Lloyd Pharmacy in system).
  - Schedule follow-up appointment with a doctor to review and assess progress.
  - Advise patient to call support to book the appointment and to monitor for red-flag symptoms.

Verbal consent from patient has been obtained before using transcription software.

Subjective:
- Presenting complaint: Acute dizziness with room-spinning sensation and unsteadiness; ears buzzing (tinnitus); nausea; unable to walk straight due to spinning.
- Onset/duration: Onset ~2 hours ago; continuous since onset.
- History: Had a similar episode about a month ago (likely shorter, ~5–10 minutes); no viral illness recently; no fever; no ear pain or discharge; hearing described as normal besides tinnitus.
- Associated symptoms: Nausea; no vomiting reported.
- Past medical history: Premature ovarian failure; on hormone replacement therapy (HRT).
- Medications: None other than HRT reported.
- Allergies: None.
- Social history: Not documented.

Objective:
- No vital signs or formal physical examination findings documented.
- No objective ear findings documented in the transcript.
- Plan to perform/obtain: blood pressure measurement; gait/stability assessment; ear examination by physician.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Labyrinthitis (vestibular vertigo suspected)
   - Assessment: Labyrinthitis suspected as the most likely diagnosis for acute vertigo with spinning sensation and tinnitus.
   - Investigations planned: 
     - Ear examination by attending physician to inspect the middle ear.
     - Blood pressure measurement.
     - Observed gait/walking assessment during waiting period.
   - Treatment planned:
     - Start an unnamed oral medication: 1 tablet three times daily; duration 10 days; route not documented.
     - Paracetamol for symptomatic relief as needed.
     - Prescription to be sent to Cross Pharmacy (Lloyd Pharmacy in system).
   - Relevant referrals: In-person ear examination by a doctor (no external specialty referral noted).
